title: Boyd Raeburn's tours and who enforced segregation
summary: Raeburn's band toured New England, Jersey and Virginia; often the proprietor, not the law, objected to a mixed band.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Where all did Boyd Raeburn's band tour?
Where all did Boy Raeburn's band tour?

Well, we toured New England, and we toured Jersey. We didn't go too far. We'd play around West Virginia and Washington, D. C. It used to be a kind of problem around there, you know. And near parts of Virginia around Washington.
They would not allow, a mixed band to appear or --

West Virginia would -- wasn't particular about it, and some places in Virginia weren't too particular about it. It was according to what place you played. Some places they didn't -- they could care less. It's the proprietor of the places where you played. It wasn't always the law. It

was -- it wasn't always the cops or something like that. It was -- a lot of times it was the proprietor. I don't know whether he'd be frightened into doing this or what. You never know where the pressure was coming from. We didn't know anyway. But he could say that we can't do it, you know. It's not the policy here. So, you couldn't stand there and argue with him and find out is it against your policy or is it the law here or what. You never got that answer anyway, so it wasn't worth it to stand around and waste your time arguing about it anyway, you know.
Because we all enjoyed playing and this was the whole scene. Huh?
